title: In general or in particulars: why the details bring G-d close
overview: "This is the chapter about the *prat*." Should the *hisbonenus* go in general, that G-d fills everything and everything is *batel* to Him, or particular by particular? The general is the real goal. But on its own it lets a person say "all is one and one is all" and understand it *mamash* backwards: G-d stays far away, and the merely general meditator can end in false visions. The particular way goes bottom-up, from what we really grasp, even if that is only our own *tevuna*, "just psychology". From the cold day and the sweater, the gas bill and the price of oranges, one follows the trail like Columbo through the *galgalim*, the angels and the *sefiros* of each world to *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, the Name *Elokim*, and then through the *partzufim* to the *Kav*. Each unification is a *prat* of a higher one; the *yichud klali* is the *bittul* of all of it to the Essence. The particular needs the general, and the general the particular, like the engineer's airplane. Every detail is aimed at the Essence; a beginner davens in general first. And for us, with two *lechatchila aribers*, the book is *Shaar HaYichud*.

terms.gloss: the general way: G-d fills everything, everything is batel to Him; it holds the real goal, but alone it sees G-d from afar

sections.title: The question: contemplate in general, or in particulars
sections.summary: Should the *hisbonenus* take G-dliness as one general idea (*derech klal*) or go through it world by world and level by level (*derech prat*)? Even the general way has many analogies and details, but they all serve one general idea, in *yichuda tata'a* and in *yichuda ila'a* alike.

phrases.he: (ד) ומעתה יש לבאר באיכות ענין ההתבוננות,
אם דרך כלל או דרך פרט דווקא,

blocks.text: "This is the chapter about the *prat*": the material has to be learned in a particular manner. The chapter asks how the *hisbonenus* (contemplation) should go: *derech klal* (the general way) or *derech prat* (the particular way).

phrases.he: כמו על דרך דוגמא בהשגה אלקית דבחינת ממלא כל עלמין,
דרך כלל בג' עולמות בי''ע,
הכל שרש ענין א' הוא
בכל המשלים דזיו והתפשטות או אותיות כו',
וכללותו רק ענין הגלוי מן ההעלם
או כמו ערך הנבדל לבחינת בעל גבול מחודש
לגבי בלתי בעל גבול דרך כלל,
שיש בזה ריבוי אופנים,
phrases.en: there's a lot of *meshalim*, even in a *derech klal*.

phrases.he: והכל בכלל,
phrases.en: which is, in general, the general thing of it;

phrases.he: גם שנמצא בזה ענינים פרטים הרבה (כמו שיתבאר)
phrases.en: and even in the *derech klal* there are a lot of different particular *inyanim*, like he's going to explain later.

blocks.text: First the general way, in *memalei kol almin*: in the three worlds of *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya* every analogy, a radiance spreading forth or letters, comes to one thing, the revelation of what is hidden. Or the general idea that the newly made, limited thing is incomparable to the limitless. "There's a lot of *meshalim* even in a *derech klal*."

In general: the *Aibershter* fills the world like the soul fills the body, or like the sun, and He is totally incomparable, like a newly made limited thing. Basically everybody is aware of these *inyanim*, if not with all the *meshalim*.

So a *derech klal* does not mean one way with no *orech*, *rochav* and *omek* (length, breadth and depth). It has many ways, all serving the general thing, and even a lot of particular *inyanim*, as he will explain later.

phrases.he: או דרך פרט,
phrases.en: Or else, whether we have to do it in a particular way:

phrases.he: להתבונן בכל עולם ובכל נברא
ובכל פרטי מדריגות חלוקים בסדרי ההשתלשלות מעילה לעילה
בכל אחד בפני עצמו דוקא כו'
phrases.en: in a particular way, each one by itself.

blocks.text: Or the particular way: to contemplate each world, each creature and every level of the chain from cause to cause, **each one by itself**. Not just that the *Aibershter* fills the world like a soul fills a body, but exactly. Everybody knows a soul fills a body; but how does it work on the eye? How does it make your tooth grow? "In a particular, particular way, each one by itself."

phrases.he: וכך הוא השאלה בהתבוננות ביחודא עילאה
באורות וכלים דאצילות
בכל פרטי עשר ספירות עד עצמות אור אין סוף
אם להתבונן בכללות ענין אור האצילות באיכות צמצומו מן העצמות ואיך שנבדל הערך לגבי עצמות המאציל ואיך דאיהו וחיוהי חד כו'
phrases.en: how in general the *sefiros* of *Atzilus* are really unified, and how the light from the infinite light is *metzumtzam* in order to come into them.

phrases.he: (גם שיש בו ענינים פרטיים הרבה מאד כמו שיתבאר)
phrases.en: And this also has a lot of *pratim*, like will be explained.

phrases.he: בכמה מיני משלים כמו שלהבת הקשורה כו' שנזכר בספר יצירה
או כענין גלוי ההעלם דכחות הנפש מעצמות הנפש דרך כלל כידוע

blocks.text: The same question is asked of *yichuda ila'a*, the lights and vessels of *Atzilus* up to the *Atzmus* (Essence) of the *Ein Sof*. In general: how the light of *Atzilus* is contracted from the *Atzmus* and incomparable to the Emanator, and how "He and His life are one", the *sefiros* really unified. This too has many *pratim* (particulars), and many analogies: the flame bound to the coal of *Sefer Yetzira*, or the soul's powers revealed from its essence.

phrases.he: עד שאחר העיון יושג בחינת העומק מזה
phrases.en: till you understand that really, in terms of the *memalei kol almin*, the worlds of *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya* are full of G-dliness, understood in a general fashion, or that the world of *Atzilus* is unified with the *Maatzil*.

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל בהשגה דממלא כל עלמין שנקרא יחודא תתאה כידוע.

blocks.text: The general way goes on until one sees its depth: that *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya* are full of G-dliness, or that *Atzilus* is unified with the Emanator. Both *yichuda ila'a* and *yichuda tata'a* can be discussed in a general manner.

What he calls a general manner is actually particular, compared to what most people think this *hisbonenus* is. "Most people, especially in our days, they don't even go this far": G-d fills everything, it's all one, or as a student put it, "the world is the universe, and the universe is the world", and they figure they *chap* it (have got it) already.

sections.title: The general way holds the goal
sections.summary: The two ways are not alike. The general way has the real advantage: it reaches the depth of the whole, the Essence of the G-dly light, which is the real goal; the details of how the letters come out of the mind are not what one is after.

phrases.he: והנה באמת לא ראי זה כו'
phrases.en: One is not really like the other.

phrases.he: דיש מעלה בהתבוננות דרך כלל
phrases.en: There really is a *maala* in the general thing.

phrases.he: כדי שיוכל לבא לבחינת העומק בכלל שהוא בחינת עצמות אור האלקי
בבחינת הכלל,
בין ביחודא עילאה בין ביחודא תתאה,
phrases.en: whether in *yichuda ila'a* or in *yichuda tata'a*: you want to understand how G-d fills up the world in *yichuda tata'a*, and how in *yichuda ila'a* the *sefiros* are unified with the *Maatzil*.

phrases.he: שזהו עיקר התכלית
phrases.en: that this is the real *tachlis*,

phrases.he: בגלוי אלקות בנפש כו'

blocks.text: In truth the two ways are not alike. The general way has a real advantage: it can reach the depth of the general, the Essence of the G-dly light. "The real thing is really *davka* in the *derech klal*."

Just as in chapter 1: why go for the *bina* (understanding) when the real thing is the *chachma* (wisdom)? Here it is the same. *Chachma* is the *klal* (the general whole) and *bina* is the *prat* (the particular), and what you are really going for is the *klal*.

**Whether in *yichuda ila'a* or in *yichuda tata'a***, you want to understand how G-d fills up the world and how the *sefiros* are unified with the Emanator. "That's what you really want." Not the particulars, like that the letters come out from *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *tevuna* and started in the *machshava iyunis* (analytical thought).

In the nitty-gritty of such *meshalim* it can seem you are not talking about G-dliness at all, but about how language is made up. "Semantics," a student offers. "No, no, there's another word for that." "Etymology." "Etymology, yeah." How the mind cuts the thing up into letters: "that's not really what you want to get to."

So the *derech klal* has a special advantage: it is about the main thing, how G-d is everywhere in everything and everything is *batel* (nullified) to the *Aibershter*. That is the real goal, the revelation of G-dliness in the soul. "The real goal that we're shooting for is the *derech klal*."

sections.title: The general alone fools a person; the particular brings G-dliness close
sections.summary: One who has only the general idea can believe he understands while G-d is far from him, and understand it the opposite of how it is. What is grasped in particulars is grasped *mamash*, even if at first it is only how things work in ourselves, and from each particular one climbs to the one above it, until the general is reached without fooling oneself.

phrases.he: ויש מעלה בהתבוננות דרך פרט דוקא
מצד עוצם הקירוב גלוי אור האלקי בנפשו יותר,
phrases.en: because this brings the revelation of the light to his soul much closer.

phrases.he: כי בהתבוננות דרך כלל יוכל להטעות את עצמו
עד שנדמה לו כי מאד קרוב אליו הדבר
phrases.en: till he can imagine himself that he really is understanding something,

phrases.he: ובאמת מרחוק מאד יהו״ה נראה לו
בהיותו דרך כלל לבד
phrases.en: since it's just a general thing, and he doesn't really know the actual particulars of how it is.

blocks.text: And the particular way has an advantage *davka*: it brings the G-dly light much closer to his soul. For in the general way he can fool himself, imagining that he really understands something.

In truth G-d appears to him from very far away. "G-d is all and all is everything and all is one" is a very vague idea, and he can take it and understand it *mamash* the opposite of how it really is, while thinking he understands it well. Why? Because it is only general, and he does not know the particulars of how it is so.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן ההתבוננות דרך פרט,
שכל פרטי בהשגה בדבר פרטי,
phrases.en: meaning to think about particular ideas, in various explanations, in particular *inyanim*:

phrases.he: הרי יוקבע בנפשו בבחינת הקירוב ביותר
phrases.en: these will come into his soul, meaning they will be connected with his mind in a very close way.

phrases.he: וממנו יבוא להשגת דבר פרטי העליון הימנו
phrases.en: And from that he can understand the level higher than that,

phrases.he: בהדרגה,
עד שיבוא לכלל ההשגה בכלליות,
phrases.en: till you can finally understand how it is in the *Chabad* of the *Or Ein Sof*.

phrases.he: שאז מתאמת יותר בלתי הטעות את עצמו כלל
phrases.en: then the thing really becomes a true *inyan* by him, without fooling himself and making mistakes.

blocks.text: Not so the particular way: each particular idea, in its explanations, is fixed in his soul in the greatest closeness, his will connected with his mind very closely.

And from it he comes to grasp the particular above it. *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *tevuna*, or how *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* comes off into the *kelipos* (the husks), he can understand very well: not a grasp of the *mahus* (what the thing is), but *mamash* an actual grasp of the *metzius* (existence).

From that he understands the level above. Even when we talk about *Atzilus*, what we really understand is *Malchus* of *tevuna*, and not of the *kelipos* in general but of our own *kelipa*. Our *meshalim* for *chachma*, *bina* and *tevuna*, the Americans and the Greeks, were really how we ourselves understand a new thing from the same *inyan*.

So what we understood is the *Chabad* of our own *kelipa*, not even of the soul but of our physical nature. And from there we can go from a particular to its general: from our *bina* to the general *bina* of the *kelipos*, then of the spiritual worlds of *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*, and on up to *Atzilus* and higher.

In chapters one to three we did not understand the whole *klal* of "His understanding is unsearchable". We understood what our own *tevuna* is, "but we understood that really good. We *mamash* understood that." Not like the guy with "all is one and one is all", who never understood how it works. We understood it well enough to turn around and explain it exactly to somebody else, and even make up new *meshalim* to fit their kind of brain.

So it almost seems: what are you talking about? This is not about *Elokus* (G-dliness), it is how the human mind works. That is "one is not like the other": it does not seem to reach the goal. "We're not trying to become psychologists over here, we're trying to understand G-dliness. And instead we're learning psychology. Yeah, we understood it very well, but it's just psychology is what it is."

But from "from my flesh I see G-d" we understand a higher *klal*, which becomes a *prat* of a higher *klal*, and so on, until he comes to the general comprehension as a whole: how it is in the *Chabad* of the *Or Ein Sof*.

What, you understand the *Chabad* of the *Or Ein Sof*? You have no idea of its *mahus* (what it is): if you *mamash* knew, you would be able to create a world. "But it doesn't matter." We understand the *metzius* (existence) of the relationship between these *inyanim*.

blocks.title: Why you want a steak
blocks.text: We learned of *Adam Kadmon* that there is no *taanug* (delight) without *ratzon* (will) and no *ratzon* without *taanug*. But we understand it by us: "Yeah, that's right, that makes sense." I want something because I enjoy it, and enjoy it because I want it. On any level, even the totally material: why do you want a steak? Because you enjoy it. And why do you enjoy it? "Because you're hungry and you want a steak."

The same works in a more refined thing, in honor or *sechel* (intellect): why do you enjoy a certain *sechel*, and why do you want it? The *ratzon* and *taanug* are *mamash* one. From the steak you go up the ladder to the *ratzon* and *taanug* of the *Atzmus*, which you *mamash* cannot understand, being part of the *Atzmus* itself, totally *hiyuli* (formless potential). Nonetheless you *mamash* understand the relationship: no *ratzon* without *taanug*, no *taanug* without *ratzon*.
"Where are we?" Then it is truer: seen this way, the thing becomes a true *inyan* by him, without fooling himself and without the mistake talked about earlier.

sections.title: Bottom-up, from the orbits to Elokim: the sweater, the gas bill and the oranges
sections.summary: The particular contemplation runs the other way from the book's explanation: from the *galgalim* and the angels up through each world's *sefiros* to *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, the Name *Elokim*. Followed link by link, from the sweater and the gas bill to the culprit, it makes G-d close and undeniable, the way an engineer, not a passenger, knows an airplane.

phrases.he: כמו כשתחלה יתבונן דרך פרט בממלא כל עלמין
באיכות התהוות שרש שפע ברוחניות דגלגלים ומזלות מאין ליש דעשיה, משמרי האופנים
phrases.en: how from the *Shemarei HaOfanim* comes out the actual physical world;

blocks.text: The example: first he contemplates in particular how the spirituality of the *galgalim* (celestial orbits) and *mazalos* (constellations) comes into being from nothing in *Asiya*, from the *Shemarei Ofanim* (the *shemarim*, dregs, of the *Ofanim*, a class of angels). This is backwards from the book: "The book is top-down. This is down-up. This is bottom-up."

The book explains top-down, but when you think it over you take it from the part you understand; and even a top-down explanation we understand down here. So once he understands how the physical world comes out of the *Shemarei Ofanim*...

phrases.he: ואחר כך יתבונן בפרטיות באופנים וחיות כו'
phrases.en: then he'll be able to understand something about the *malachim*,

phrases.he: עד בחינת מלכות דעשיה,
phrases.en: till from there he can understand the next level up, which is where the *heichalos* are in the *Malchus* of *Asiya*,

phrases.he: כללות האור האלקי שמהוה עולם העשיה
ועל דרך זה בפרטי י׳ ספירות דעשיה
phrases.en: so then, once you understand how it is in *Malchus* of *Asiya*, you can understand higher and higher, into *Yesod* of *Asiya*, all the way up to *Keser* of *Asiya*,

phrases.he: עד בחינת מלכות דיצירה שנעשה כתר לעשיה
וכן על דרך זה בפרטיות דיצירה
phrases.en: and then in the same way you can go up the ladder, like Jacob's ladder,

phrases.he: ובפרטיות דבריאה כו'

blocks.text: Then he contemplates the particulars of the *Ofanim* and the *Chayos*, and understands something about the angels; from there the next level up, the inner part of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, where the chambers are: the whole of the G-dly light that brings the world of *Asiya* into being.

So too through the ten *sefiros* of *Asiya*: from *Malchus* of *Asiya* higher and higher up to *Keser* of *Asiya*, and from there to the inner part of *Malchus* of *Yetzira*, which becomes the *Keser* of *Asiya*.

So too through the particulars of *Yetzira*, and then of *Beriya*: up the ladder, "like Jacob's ladder". This is the *inyan* of *tefilla* (prayer) too: *hisbonenus* is *avoda* (divine service), *avoda* is *tefilla*, and *tefilla* is to go up the ladder.

phrases.he: עד בחינת מלכות דאצילות
phrases.en: and all the way up to *Malchus* of *Atzilus*,

phrases.he: כללות הכל כו'
phrases.en: which includes the whole entire external worlds of *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*,

phrases.he: שנקרא שם אלהי״ם בכלל כידוע

blocks.text: **Up to *Malchus* of *Atzilus***: to *Keser* of *Beriya*, and then how *Malchus* of *Atzilus* becomes *Keser* of *Beriya*. *Malchus* of *Atzilus* is the whole, including all of *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*, and that is *yichuda tata'a*.

He is not talking about the explanation here, which goes from up to down, but about seeing it: "Lift up your eyes on high". Once you have the explanation in particular, you can literally look at the world.

blocks.title: I have to wear a sweater because of the galgalim
blocks.text: It's cold today; it's winter. Why? Because we are in that part of the *mazalos*, with the turnings of the *galgalim*, that makes it winter, and the leaves fall, "and that's why I have to wear a sweater." "Wow, look at that. I have to wear a sweater because of the *galgalim*." Now this is *mamash* affecting me.

blocks.title: The gas bill
blocks.text: Not only that: money. "Right now, my heater is on. And the bill is going to hit me at the end of the month." "We're talking now about my pocketbook." I could buy stuff with that money, and the *galgalim* and *mazalos* are causing it to go on gas. "My money!" A totally physical being can see this affecting him: the sweater, the earmuffs, the heat.

blocks.title: From the guy next door to Israel and the Arabs
blocks.text: That is *mamash* my own life. Then the *klal*: if it affects me, it affects the guy next door, so all of Pittsburgh, so all of northern America, so the whole price of gas, so the price of energy, so it could have something to do with Israel and the Arabs. "You go up from level to level with the *pratim*." And what is affecting all of that? The *galgalim*: which *mazal* we are under.

"Okay, where are we now?" From here you go up and up: from the *galgalim* to the *Ofanim*, to *Malchus* of *Asiya*, all the way to *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, which includes all the external worlds of *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya* and is called, in general, the Name *Elokim*.

phrases.he: שאז מתאמת הדבר יותר בקירוב כו',
כי אחר העיון היטב בכל הפרטים,
הגם שכל פרט בפני עצמו אינו ענין אלהות בכללות
phrases.en: even though each particular *prat* is not an *inyan* of *Elokus* in general,

phrases.he: ואינו רק בחינת טפל פרטי לבד,
phrases.en: it's just a particular, a secondary; not even a secondary, it's not the main thing.

phrases.he: אבל כאשר יתחבר כל העיון מכל הפרטים אל הכלל,
phrases.en: once you put the whole thing together with all the *pratim*,

phrases.he: אז יוקבע יותר בנפש בחינת הכלל
phrases.en: but *davka* when you know all the *pratim*, then you really know the *klal*,

phrases.he: כאשר בדוק ומנוסה לכל עוסק בעמקות בהתבוננות
phrases.en: like this is already tested and tried, to anybody who really has done the proper, deepest *hisbonenus*.

blocks.text: "Then the thing truly comes out close." I say: G-d is affecting the fact that my gas bill is high. Whose fault is that? It's the Name *Elokim*. "It's not just a coincidence."

blocks.title: Who got me the orange
blocks.text: On *Shabbos* we had some real good food. Where did it come from? The sun, the moon, the water and the earth, and those depend on the year: a drought one year, a frost another, and the oranges got expensive. Who did that? Everybody says, "Oh, the *Aibershter* is giving us the oranges." But here I am "following the trail of how exactly the *Aibershter* is giving me oranges."

blocks.title: Columbo finds the culprit
blocks.text: "The *Aibershter* didn't give me the orange, I bought it in the store." Yes, but the *galgalim* affect how much money you have and what oranges cost. Who affects the *galgalim*? The angels. And the angels? *Malchus* of *Asiya*. You follow the trail up like Columbo and find out who done it: "the culprit of everything is the *Aibershter*, is *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, *Elokim*."
Then the thing truly comes out close, and nobody can spin me a tale and convince me there is no G-d. "What do you mean? I can show you the whole trail, how G-d got me the orange."

Yet each particular by itself is not G-dliness as a whole; it could be no *inyan* of *Elokus* at all. The first *prat* was the sweater because it is cold outside. What does that have to do with *Elokus*? It is only a *tefel*. "How do you say *tefel* in English? Secondary." Not even secondary: why would you even talk about it? "We want to talk about G-d and you're talking about your sweater and your gas bill."

blocks.title: The airplane engineer
blocks.text: But when all the particulars are joined to the general, "you have an airplane." Who didn't hear of an airplane? Everybody knows what it is. Yes, but the engineer knows every little screw and where it goes, and all its aerodynamics. He *mamash* knows what the airplane is all about.

blocks.title: Go and make an airplane
blocks.text: Why can an airplane fly? "Well, it has wings." Good: go and make one. You make a thing with wings, throw it, and it falls down. The engineer knows exactly how the wings make it fly. Here too, not just "there's a G-d in the world and He makes it work", like the propeller and the wings: you know each little part particularly.

blocks.title: Algebra class, and the ABC before the needle
blocks.text: Each part is only a particular. The engineer goes to the screw class, the propeller class, the aerodynamics class, and in his algebra class: "I want to be an airplane guy and you're teaching me algebra." The little kid who wants to be a doctor gets "A, B, C, D, E, F, G." "What do you mean? Give me a needle and I'll start sticking people." "No, first you have to learn all the *pratim*."

So though each is only a *prat*, when all are joined to the general, the general is fixed in the soul. The real thing is *davka* the *klal*, but only knowing all the *pratim* do you really know it, as anyone who has done the deepest *hisbonenus* has tested and tried.

sections.title: The higher unity in particulars, and the delusions of the merely general
sections.summary: In *yichuda ila'a* too, knowing how each *partzuf* comes from the one above it, up to the *Kav*, the *tzimtzum* and the infinite light, fixes the Emanator's Essence in the soul; "there's a G-d and finished" sees Him from afar. Whoever squeezes his whole mind onto one vague general idea can fall into false imaginings, while the same depth of *daas* poured into each particular is the opposite of error.

phrases.he: וגם ביחודא עילאה
phrases.en: And it's the same by *yichuda ila'a*:

phrases.he: בהתבוננות דרך פרט
phrases.en: when you know it in a particular way,

phrases.he: בכל פרטי העשר ספירות
בפרצופים דזעיר אנפין ונוקבא ואבא ואמא ואריך אנפין ועתיק יומין
עד ראשית הקו באדם קדמון כו'
דרך פרט דוקא,
phrases.en: to know the whole thing in particular

phrases.he: הוא המועיל לקבוע בנפש מבחינת כללות עצמות המאציל
הכוללם יחד
phrases.en: that includes everything.

blocks.text: So too in *yichuda ila'a*: know in particular the ten *sefiros* and the *partzufim* (statures of the *sefiros*), *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*, *Abba* and *Ima*, *Arich Anpin* and *Atik Yomin*, how each works and connects with the next. Not "well, *Zeir Anpin*, it's the light of G-d", but exactly how *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva* come from *Abba* and *Ima*, and those from *Arich* and *Atik*, up to *Adam Kadmon*, as in chapter 18.
*Davka* knowing everything in particular fixes in the soul the whole of the Essence of the Emanator, which includes them all. That is what you really wanted to know, not even *Malchus* of *Atzilus*.

From *Malchus* of *Atzilus* to the unions of *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*, then of *Abba* and *Ima*, then down from *Arich* and *Atik*, which come from *Adam Kadmon*, to the beginning of the line; then how the line comes after the impression left by the *tzimtzum*, and before it the *tzimtzum* and the infinite light.

Then it is not just "there's an infinite light." What's that? "Well, it's, you know, like a light bulb you have, it's a big light bulb." That is how they understand it. And what do you need all these *partzufim* for? "There's a G-d, and there's a G-d, and finished." No: knowing the things **in a particular way**, *davka*, is what brings the soul to the whole of the Essence of the Emanator.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן ההתבוננות דרך כלל לבד
phrases.en: But it's not like that when the *hisbonenus* is just, "Well, there's a G-d in the world":

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל
שמרחוק יהו״ה נראה לו
phrases.en: then he sees G-d from very, very far away,

phrases.he: (עד שיוכל ליפול בדמיונות כוזבות כשוטים וחסרי הדעת
phrases.en: then he can fall into total *avoda zara* things, like the idiots and the *chasrei daas*,

phrases.he: מצד צמצום כלי מוחו רק בדבר א'
phrases.en: because he is concentrating his whole brain into just one thing,

phrases.he: והוא כללי כו')
phrases.en: and this is just a general, vague *inyan*.

blocks.text: Not so the general way alone, a *hisbonenus* of just "well, there's a G-d in the world": G-d appears to him from afar, very, very far away.
Until he can fall into false imaginings, like fools and those who lack *daas*: then he can fall into total *avoda zara* (idolatry) things, "like the idiots and the *chasrei daas*".

sensitivity.reason: Says the merely general meditator can fall into "total avoda zara things, like the idiots", of people who practise such meditation.
sensitivity.publishable: **Until he can fall into false imaginings, like fools and those who lack *daas***.

blocks.text: After the tape is turned: what do these people do? "They sit and they meditate on the *omka d'chula*," the depth of everything, that there is a G-d and He is infinite, and they *mamash* have visions: false imaginations, "like the total idiots".

sensitivity.reason: Calls people who practise this kind of meditation, and have visions from it, "total idiots".
sensitivity.publishable: After the tape is turned: what do such people do? They sit and meditate on the *omka d'chula*, the depth of everything, that there is a G-d and He is infinite, and they *mamash* have visions: false imaginations, of the kind the text calls foolish.

blocks.text: Why? Because he contracts the vessels of his mind into only one thing, concentrating his whole brain on a single general, vague *inyan*.

phrases.he: אבל צמצום העמקת הדעת בכל פרט
הוא ההיפוך מן הטעות
phrases.en: That is the opposite from making mistakes,

phrases.he: והריחוק
phrases.en: and from seeing it only in a faraway, vague way.

phrases.he: אדרבא,
phrases.en: Just the opposite:

phrases.he: על ידי זה מתקרב הדבר יותר אצלו בהיותו הולך מפרט לפרט העליון הימנו
עד שכוללם יחד, ליחד יחוד כללי
phrases.en: till he connects all of them in a general unification,

phrases.he: ולא יחוד פרטי
כמו לך יהו״ה הגדולה כו'

blocks.question: "Wait a minute": chapter 1 said *amkus hadaas* (depth of *daas*) is the *kli* (vessel) for everything. Is this not the same?
blocks.text: Yes, but not *amkus hadaas* to sit and meditate on the final *klal*. You have *hisbonenus* and *amkus hadaas* in every *prat*: learning this *prat*, you are totally concentrated on it and no other.

That is the opposite of mistake and of distance, of a faraway, vague view you do not understand and can turn upside down. Going from each *prat* to the one above, he connects them all in a general unification and knows the thing with all its *pratim*, like a doctor knows the body, or the engineer the airplane.
Like "Yours, G-d, is the greatness." Now he explains what a *yichud prati* (particular unification) is and what a *yichud klali* (general unification) is.

sections.title: Particular unifications, and the one general unification
sections.summary: Following one attribute, like *chesed*, through every world is only a *yichud prati*, and taking one attribute for the whole is a mistake. Each unification is only a detail of a higher one; the *yichud klali* is the *bittul* of the whole chain of the *Kav* to the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*.

phrases.he: שענין היחוד האלקי הוא בחינת עומק ההשגה
בביטול היש לאין
phrases.en: the nullification of the *yesh* of the *pratim* to the total *ayin* of understanding the whole thing together,

phrases.he: ביחודא עילאה ויחודא תתאה

blocks.text: The G-dly unification is the depth of comprehension. A *yichud prati* is, for instance, that of *gedula* (greatness): *Malchus* of *Asiya* connected to *Malchus* of *Yetzira*, that to *Malchus* of *Beriya*, and so on up to *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*. Beyond that, he connects all the particular unifications to G-d Himself.
That is the *bittul* of the *yesh* (something) to the *ayin* (nothing), in *yichuda ila'a* and *yichuda tata'a*: the *yesh* of the *pratim* nullified to the total *ayin* of the whole together.

phrases.he: ויש יחוד פרטי
בדבר פרטי,
כמו לך יהו״ה הגדולה
שהוא בחינת חסד שבמלכות דאצילות בבי''ע דרך פרט בכל עולם כו'
phrases.en: to understand how *chesed* of *Atzilus* comes into the *chasadim* of *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*, in each particular world.

phrases.he: וגם כללותו אינו אלא פרט
phrases.en: Even when you understand the whole thing, it is only a *prat*:

phrases.he: מדה א' ממדה שבמלכות כו'
phrases.en: meaning *chesed* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus*.

blocks.text: A particular unification in a particular thing: "Yours, G-d, is the greatness" is the *chesed* in *Malchus* of *Atzilus*. How it comes into the *chassadim* (kindnesses) of each of *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya* is only a unification of the *chassadim*.

And even the whole of it is only a particular, and taking it for the whole is still a mistake, "like, you know, the people who say G-d is love." If G-d is love, why do so many bad things happen? What happened to justice?

sensitivity.reason: "The people who say G-d is love" points, without naming it, at another religion's creed, as an example of a mistake.
sensitivity.publishable: **And even the whole of it is only a particular**, and taking it for the whole is still a mistake. Say that G-d is only love: then why do so many bad things happen? What happened to justice?

blocks.text: Why? They follow one *prat* and take it as the *klal*. Knowing only the *chassadim*, the right line and not the left, you cannot put them together to go the next step higher. It is a *prat* of one attribute, *chesed* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus*; and so with *gevura*.

phrases.he: ולך יהו״ה הגבורה
phrases.en: The same thing in terms of *gevura*

phrases.he: בכללותו ופרטיו בכל עולם נקרא יחוד פרטי
ועל דרך זה בכל יחודים פרטיים שבי׳ ספירות דבי''ע כידוע

blocks.text: *Gevura* too, whole and in particulars in each world, is a *yichud prati*, and so all the particular unifications of the ten *sefiros*. You learn the *pratim*, then their unifications, till you unify all the *sefiros* of the upper worlds with the same *sefiros* below.

phrases.he: אבל יחוד הכללי הוא כמו מה שכתוב
הנה מקום אתי
phrases.en: There's a place with Me: the whole place of the world is by Me;

phrases.he: או המלך המרומם כו'
phrases.en: that the *Aibershter* is a King of the whole world;

phrases.he: המתנשא מכל ימות עולם דו׳ קצוות ומוחין חכמה ובינה שבהם כו'
phrases.en: how the actual *Aibershter* is totally higher than even the whole ten *sefiros*, and even the ten *sefiros atzmiyim*.

phrases.he: וגם זה פרט יחשב
phrases.en: And even this will be considered a *prat*

phrases.he: לגבי עצמות בחינת המלכות שהוא כתר מל'
phrases.en: compared to the actual inner part of *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, which is the *Keser* of *Malchus*.

blocks.text: But the general unification is "Behold, there is a place with Me": the whole place of the world is by Me. To understand that a world is nothing but G-dliness, and really understand what that means.
That is, "not according to the *avoda zara* (idolatry) means".

sensitivity.reason: Calls the other understanding of "the world is nothing but G-dliness" (the world itself as G-d, as other religions or pantheism hold) idolatry. The remark is the point (which reading he means), so it is published as said.

blocks.text: Or "the exalted King": the *Aibershter* is King of the whole world, "raised above all the days of the world", the six directions and the *mochin*, *chachma* and *bina*, in them. The *Aibershter* is totally higher than the whole ten *sefiros*, even the ten essential *sefiros*.

And even this is a particular. Within *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, the King is totally higher than its separate ten *sefiros*, and even that is only a *prat* compared to the inner part of *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, **which is the *Keser* of *Malchus***.

phrases.he: וכה"ג בע"ס דאצי' כו'
phrases.en: The same way in the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*: besides the *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, you go higher and higher in *Atzilus*,

phrases.he: עד עצמות בחינת מלכות דאין סוף בראשית הקו,
phrases.en: till you go all the way up to the *yichudim* of unifying everything into *Malchus* of *Ein Sof* in the beginning of the *Kav*.

phrases.he: יש יחודים פרטים הרבה בכל ספירה ופרצוף כו'
phrases.en: There's all kinds of different details, and unifications of the details.

phrases.he: ויחוד הכללי בכללות ביטול כל ההשתלשלות דקו כו'
phrases.en: And then the *yichud hakelali*, finally, after this whole thing, is the *bittul* of the whole *hishtalshelus* of the *Kav*

phrases.he: לגבי עצמות אור אין סוף כידוע.
phrases.en: to the *Atzmus* of the *Or Ein Sof*, as is known.

blocks.text: So too through the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*, higher and higher, up to the Essence of *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* at the beginning of the *Kav*, unifying everything into it. Every *sefira* and *partzuf* has many particular unifications, and each is a detail compared to the *klal* above it: "even when you make a whole big unification, it's still only a detail compared to the next level up."
Finally, after all of this, the general unification is the *bittul* of the whole chain of descent of the *Kav* to the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*, as is known.

sections.title: The particular needs the general, and the general needs the particular
sections.summary: Whoever starts from the general, however hard he works at it, will not have its truth fixed in him like one who reaches it through the particulars. But particulars never put together are no better: the blind men and the elephant. The *Rishonim* already disagreed about the same thing in prayer.

phrases.he: אך הנה מי שלא העמיק דעתו ביחודים פרטים
ומתחיל מבחינת הכלל,
גם שבא לו ביגיעה רבה בהשגות רבות
phrases.en: that he doesn't just say, "Well, everything just comes from the infinite light," but he thinks, like a soul in the body and like the flame from a coal, and he thinks about it really hard:

phrases.he: באיכות ענין הביטול בכלל,
phrases.en: how exactly this *bittul* is,

phrases.he: כמו כשלהבת כו' וכהאי גוונא,
לא יוקבע בנפשו אמיתית ענינו כל כך,
phrases.en: really the real way how it is will not really be entrenched in his soul, or in his mind,

phrases.he: כמו אחר עיון היטב בכל פרטיים,
phrases.en: like the real *iyun* in all the particular *prat*,

phrases.he: עד שמהם יבוא לבחינת בכלל.
phrases.en: till it comes from them to the *klal*.

blocks.text: But one who has not delved into the particular unifications and starts from the general, "everything comes from the infinite light", even with great toil and many comprehensions, thinking hard of a soul in the body or the flame from a coal and how exactly this *bittul* is: the truth of it will not be entrenched in his soul as after a good *iyun* in all the particulars, coming from them to the general.

phrases.he: והיינו דפרט אצטריך לכלל וכלל אצטריך לפרט,
מפני שאין כלל בלא פרט כו'
phrases.en: There's no such thing as a *klal* without a *prat*, or a *prat* without a *klal*.

blocks.text: The particular needs the general and the general the particular. You cannot get totally hung up on the *pratim*; you have to unify them into a *klal*. "A guy who just knows what the screws are and doesn't know how they go together will never be able to make an airplane, either."

blocks.title: The blind men and the elephant
blocks.text: Like the seven blind men with the elephant: one thought an elephant is like a palm tree, another like a broom, because none realized he held only a *prat*. So the way of the *prat* alone is not good either.
"And this is, by the way, the way of the scientists": they learned the *pratim* and never tried to put them together into a *klal*, and so they think the *pratim* somehow work by themselves.

sensitivity.reason: A sweeping remark about scientists as a group: they only collect details and think the details work by themselves.
sensitivity.publishable: This is the way of anyone who learns the *pratim* and never puts them together into a *klal*: he ends up thinking the *pratim* somehow work by themselves.

blocks.text: For there is no *klal* without a *prat*, and no *prat* without a *klal*. To understand a thing properly you must know all its *pratim*, and then you can understand the *klal*.

phrases.he: (ודבר זה כבר נחלקו בו הרבה מגדולי הראשונים כמו הרמב''ם והטור,
אם לכוון בפירוש המלות דרך פרט בגדלות יהו״ה,
phrases.en: Are you supposed to think, when you say *Lecha Hashem hagedula*, of *gedula*, and when you say *hagevura*, of *gevura*, etc., in all the *kavanos*,

phrases.he: אם לכוון דרך כלל, לפני מי אתה עומד ומתפלל כו'
phrases.en: or whether you should just think, "I'm standing in front of the *Aibershter*"?

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בכתבים)

blocks.question: In prayer, should you think of the particular meaning of each word, or only "before Whom you stand"?
blocks.text: This is the *avoda* of *tefilla*, the whole *inyan* of *hisbonenus* and going up, and great *Rishonim* (early authorities) like the *Rambam* and the Tur already disagreed about it. Saying "Yours, G-d, is the greatness", do you think of *gedula*, at "the might" of *gevura*, and so through all the *kavanos* (intentions)? Or just: I am standing in front of the *Aibershter*?

sections.title: Every particular aimed at the Essence
sections.summary: A general and a particular thought cannot be held at once, but whoever wants only the Essence directs every particular to it, more truly than one who thinks of the Essence directly. The particulars, even when they look like psychology, are studied only to reach Him, never as a subject for itself, and so too the *Zohar* and the *Arizal*, as the Alter Rebbe heard from the *Maggid*.

phrases.he: והגם שהמחשבה כללית עם המחשבה פרטית לא ישכנו כאחד,
phrases.en: The general *machshava* with the particular *machshava* cannot: you can't think about two things at once.

phrases.he: מכל מקום מי שהוא מעמיק בכל לבו ובכל חפצו לעצמות האלקות דוקא,
phrases.en: since we're *ma'amik* with all the heart and desire to the *Atzmus Elokus*, *davka*,

phrases.he: הנה גם בעיונו בפרטיות יכוין הכל אל המחשבה הכללית דעצמות דוקא
phrases.en: even when it seems like we're talking about human psychology, we know that's not at all what we're talking about, but the *kavana* is *mamash* to the *Atzmus*.

blocks.text: A general and a particular thought cannot dwell together: you cannot think two things at once. Thinking before Whom you stand, you think of that; thinking of *Malchus* of *tevuna*, you think of that.

Nevertheless, one who delves with all his heart and desire *davka* to the Essence of G-dliness will direct even his *iyun* in the particulars to it. Now we learn one *prat*, *bina*, now another, *chachma*; it seems like human psychology, "but the *kavana* is *mamash* to the *Atzmus*." Not only that: his thought is more on the *Atzmus* than that of somebody intending the *Atzmus* itself.

phrases.he: ולא יפול מכללות הכונה כלל
phrases.en: And the *klalus* of the *kavana* will not go at all

phrases.he: מחמת צמצום הכונה הפרטיות,
phrases.en: from the fact that you're just talking about little particular details,

phrases.he: מאחר שכל הפרטים אינם נמשכים והולכים רק אחר הכלל דוקא,
phrases.en: since all the *pratim* that he's talking about and thinking about go totally only after the *klal* of the *Aibershter* Himself,

phrases.he: כידוע לכל הולך בדרך אמת,
phrases.en: like is known to anybody who learns the proper way:

phrases.he: ליהו״ה לבדו דוקא,
phrases.en: *davka* to the *Aibershter*.

phrases.he: כמו שכתבו זכרונם לברכה אליו ולא למדותיו
phrases.en: Like they said: our whole *kavana* in this whole study is *davka* to the *Aibershter* Himself, and has nothing to do with the *middos* at all.

blocks.text: And he will not fall at all from the whole of the *kavana*. Little particular details, which are really not even *tevuna*, *bina*, *chachma* or *Malchus* of *Atzilus* but our own particular *kelipa*, do not disturb the *kavana* to the *Aibershter* Himself. Since we are truly aimed at Him, just the opposite: "It's what makes the *kavana* proper."

For all the particulars he thinks about go only after the *klal*, the *Aibershter* Himself, as is known to anyone going the true way, *davka* to Him, as the Sages said: "to Him, and not to His attributes." Our whole *kavana* in this study is *davka* to the *Aibershter* Himself, nothing to do with the *middos*.

phrases.he: רק כללות ענין ההתבוננות בפרטי מדותיו
הוא רק כדי שיבא לעצמותו ומהותו דוקא
ולא לכוון העיקר רק בכוונה של הפרט,
phrases.en: And it's not that we're having any *kavana* in terms of a *prat*,

phrases.he: כמו בשביל איזה לימוד לעצמו.
phrases.en: like a person who wants to learn something for himself.

blocks.text: Contemplating the particulars of His attributes is only so that he come to His Essence and *mahus*: that is what we intend. Not the particular for itself, like a person who wants to learn something for himself.

Like an etymologist or a psychologist, who wants to learn what *bina* and *chachma* are, and that is what he learns. "What we're learning has nothing to do with *bina* and *chachma* at all, we're learning about the *Aibershter*."

phrases.he: גם בעיונו בספר הזוהר ובכתבי האריז''ל
phrases.en: Even when he's looking in the *Zohar*, in the *Arizal*,

phrases.he: צריך להיות על דרך זה דוקא
phrases.en: it all has to be *davka* like this.

phrases.he: ודי למבין
phrases.en: And this is enough to understand.

phrases.he: (וכאשר מקובל היה אבי אדוני מורי ורבי זכרונו לברכה נשמתו עדן בדבר זה מפי הרב המגיד זכרונו לברכה בפירוש גמור וכך שמעתי מפיו זכרונו לברכה)
phrases.en: I heard from my father that he said he learned this from the *Maggid*, with a *perush gamur*.

blocks.text: So too in studying the *Zohar* and the writings of the *Arizal*, not "like some people want to look in the *Zohar* to find out about demons or something like that." It must all be *davka* this way, "and this is enough for one who understands."

"As my father received on this matter from the mouth of the Rav, the *Maggid*": the *Mitteler Rebbe* says he heard from his father, the Alter Rebbe, that he learned this from the *Maggid* as an explicit explanation.

sections.title: Kabbalistic meanings do not confuse the general; the beginner; lechatchila ariber
sections.summary: The particular, Kabbalistic meanings do not confuse the general thought; they strengthen it, whatever the complaints against "our way". A beginner davens before the *Aibershter* in general and grows into the particulars. And for us, after the Rebbe's two *lechatchila aribers*, this is not a tract on contemplation but *Shaar HaYichud*, the beginning of the work of *Moshiach*: to know G-d.

phrases.he: ובזה מתורץ שאלת השואלים על פירוש המלות דרך פרט
phrases.en: And this explains what they ask about this:

phrases.he: ליודעים בהם,
איך שאינם מבלבלים את מחשבת הכלל
phrases.en: that this does not make a *bilbul* in the understanding of G-dliness,

phrases.he: אלא אדרבא
phrases.en: just the opposite.

phrases.he: כוונות פירוש המלות על פי המלות עפ"י הקבלה
מסייעים לחזק את עומק השגת הכלל בעצמות אלקות,
כידוע לטועמי טעם בהם דרך פרט כו'
phrases.en: Like is known to anybody who really tasted the taste of this learning, in a particular way.

blocks.text: This answers those who ask about the meanings of the words in particular, for those who know them: how do they not confuse the general thought? We do not yet *daven* with the meanings, but about how we study, a lot of people think: what are you studying? The main thing is *ein od milvado* (there is nothing besides Him). You are just *maskilim* (people of intellect) after Kabbalistic matters, *razi li* (my secret is mine), to know all kinds of particular things.

"No, it's not like that," and the *Mitteler Rebbe* has it from his father, who had it from the *Maggid*. It makes no confusion in understanding G-dliness; just the opposite, the Kabbalistic meaning of the words strengthens the depth of the comprehension of the general, in the Essence of G-dliness.

"What do you need to learn Kabbalistic matters? The main thing is there's a G-d, *ein od milvado*." "This is one of the big complaints against our way, you know." As is known to anybody who has really tasted the taste of this learning, in a particular way.

phrases.he: רק החדשים
phrases.en: But the new people to this thing:

phrases.he: יותר טוב להם להעמיק דרך כלל תחלה,
phrases.en: when you're *davenen*, just *daven* like you're in front of the *Aibershter*,

phrases.he: עד שיורגלו מעט מעט בדרך הפרט דווקא
phrases.en: until you learn a little bit better, and then you'll be able, even in the *davenen*, also to *daven* like this.

phrases.he: ודי למבין:
phrases.en: And this is enough for a person to understand.

blocks.question: So how should we *daven* (pray)? Should we start *davenen* by the *kavanos* of the *Arizal*?
blocks.text: No. For those new to this, it is better to stand in the general way first, until little by little they get used to the particular way. When you *daven*, just *daven* as if you are in front of the *Aibershter*, until you learn a little better; then you can *daven* like this too. "And this is enough for one who understands."

blocks.title: Lechatchila ariber: like Rashbi, who did not have to daven
blocks.text: Here we should mention *lechatchila ariber* (over the top from the start). The Rebbe said that by us we can go *lechatchila ariber*, "and he really meant *lechatchila ariber*, *lechatchila ariber*", on top of the one the *Rebbe Maharash* said: straight to living like *Moshiach*, "and we don't even have to worry about *davenen*", like Rashbi, who did not have to *daven*.

sensitivity.reason: "We don't even have to worry about davenen", taken out of the class, reads as license not to pray; he means that the learning itself is already directed to the Essence.
sensitivity.publishable: Here we should mention *lechatchila ariber* (over the top from the start). The Rebbe said that by us we can go *lechatchila ariber*, "and he really meant *lechatchila ariber*, *lechatchila ariber*", on top of the one the *Rebbe Maharash* said: straight to living like *Moshiach*, the learning itself, like Rashbi's, already directed straight to the Essence.

blocks.title: Choni HaMe'agel davened; Rashbi said Chassidus
blocks.text: Rashbi just learned; he did not have to *daven*. Choni HaMe'agel *davened* and got the rain; Rashbi just said *Chassidus*, and the rain came. So by us we can go totally beyond, not even think of bringing the *Chassidus* into the *davenen*: *lechatchila ariber*, straight to *daas Havaya* (knowing G-d), "even without *davenen*", intending the *Atzmus* directly in the learning. The whole thing is one.

sensitivity.reason: Continues the point that "even without davenen" the learning suffices; a reader could take it as a rule about prayer.
sensitivity.publishable: Rashbi just learned. Choni HaMe'agel *davened* and got the rain; Rashbi just said *Chassidus*, and the rain came. So by us we can go *lechatchila ariber*, straight to *daas Havaya* (knowing G-d), intending the *Atzmus* directly in the learning itself. The whole thing is one.

blocks.text: For these are already the days of *Moshiach*. The *davenen* he speaks of here means first the learning, of the *inyanim* and the *pratim*, then the *amkus hadaas* into them, to make the *kavana* in the *davenen* a *kavana* to the *Atzmus*: that is *avodas halev* (the service of the heart). And the Rebbe said already: we are *lechatchila ariber*.

blocks.title: Two lechatchila aribers: depth within depth
blocks.text: The *Rebbe Maharash*'s *lechatchila ariber* meant *avodas hamochin* (the service of the mind). The Rebbe said a second one even on that, *omek lifnim m'omek* (depth within depth): not just a second depth like the first, but depth in relation to the first.

blocks.title: The guy polishing his car
blocks.text: The Rebbe said we are in the days of *Moshiach*, and explained the *Rambam*: then the occupation of the whole world will be only to know G-d, and the world full of that knowledge as the waters cover the sea. Even some guy polishing his car in the corner, a *prat* that seems opposite to the *klal*, "a *kelipa*, a bad *kelipa*", is *mamash ein od milvado*, nothing but the *Aibershter* Himself, understood properly. Not from far away, that the world is G-d, "which is a really pantheistic nonsense".

We are very lucky to be learning this book. People say, "Oh, you're *chassidim* of the *Mitteler Rebbe*." "It's not true. We are *chassidim* of the Rebbe." Next to the *Mitteler Rebbe*'s *chassidim*, "we're like, I wouldn't even say babies, we're like amoebas": if they were angels, we are people; if people, we are donkeys. "And yet you see that by them they didn't get it like we do."

sensitivity.reason: Answers people who call us "chassidim of the Mitteler Rebbe" ("It's not true"), and says the Mitteler Rebbe's chassidim "did not get it the way we do": a claim about other approaches within Chabad.
sensitivity.publishable: We are very lucky to be learning this book, and we are *chassidim* of the Rebbe. Next to the *Mitteler Rebbe*'s *chassidim*, "we're like, I wouldn't even say babies, we're like amoebas": if they were angels, we are people; if people, we are donkeys.

blocks.text: Why do we get it as they did not? Because we are students of the Rebbe, with two *lechatchila aribers* on it: the *Rebbe Maharash* made one, and the Rebbe made another on top of his.

So by us this is no longer *Kuntres HaHisbonenus*, a tract on contemplation, as they used to call it. It is *Shaar HaYichud*, and if it is a tract, "we should call it" the tract of *daas Havaya*, knowing G-d. For by us the *avoda* of *Moshiach* has started, when the occupation of the whole world will be only to know G-d. "That's all we're interested in over here. And that's the end of the chapter," and this is enough for one who understands.

reviewQuestions.question: What is the advantage of the general way, and why does the chapter call it the real goal?
How can one who says "all is one and one is all" understand G-dliness the opposite of how it is, and why does the particular way not fall into this?
Why does the particular contemplation go bottom-up, and how does the trail from a sweater or a gas bill lead to the Name *Elokim*?
Why is following *chesed* through all the worlds still only a *yichud prati*, and what is the *yichud klali*?
What do the airplane engineer and the blind men with the elephant each show about the particular and the general?
If a general and a particular thought cannot be held together, how can study of the particulars be directed to the Essence, and how should a beginner *daven*?

"Hold on, I got to change phones, the crew is here": a phone change mid-sentence.

After "that's the end of the chapter" the side holds a few sentences with long gaps, in another voice and style ("we cannot learn like a doctor studies medicine... Torah as the prism"): not this class.

notes.text: Line 16 is aligned late (022 w2028, conf 0.477): he reads its first words at w1296 and its end at w2028, with the long explanation of what "our own kelipa" understands in between. Lines 15 and 16 are one passage for that reason.

He refers back to the Americans and the Greeks (a mashal from the earlier chapters) and to a class "when we learned in א"ק" on taanug and ratzon; the blocks say only what he says here. The second reference is probably to the classes on chapters 10-15, recorded first.
Line 24: the end of his reading is garbled in the transcript ("עד ריש ועקב עקב בא״ק, like the ענין in chapter 18"); the block keeps only "up to Adam Kadmon, like the inyan in chapter 18".
Line 21: the transcript has him say "till you get to Keser of Beriya" while reading "up to Malchus of Atzilus"; it is his ascent (Malchus of Atzilus becomes Keser of Beriya), kept as said.
Line 42: he does not say which of the Rambam and the Tur held which view, and the block does not either.

The Choni HaMe'agel and Rashbi story is told as he told it ("Rashbi just said Chassidus and the rain came"); no source is given in class. The lechatchila ariber digression, earlier left out of the ported draft, is kept here and flagged; he should be asked how he wants it read.
